summary: A text field that filters a list, with any number of values chosen. The choices show as removable tags beneath the field and are read with it.
useWhen: the user picks several values from a list too long to show as checkboxes — teams, regions, labels, assignees
a table filter can match more than one value — "Status is Failing or Paused"

useInstead.why: Combobox's input shows the chosen label; here the input only ever holds the filter text, and the list stays open for the next pick

useInstead.when: there are about seven options or fewer
useInstead.why: every option visible at once beats typing to find one, and nothing is hidden behind a popover

useInstead.when: the values are free text the user invents, not options from a list
useInstead.why: MultiSelect only chooses from `options`; a free-text tag input is a TagGroup beside an Input

composition.note: Pass the full `options` list; filtering, the tags and the announcement are the component's. In a table's filter bar, give it `aria-label` and `hideTags`, and list its values in the table's active-filters TagGroup — one removable tag per value, not the same tags twice.
composition.example: <MultiSelect label="Notify teams" options={teams} value={teamIds} onChange={setTeamIds} placeholder="Search teams" />

label.note: names the field and the tags beneath it

emptyLabel.note: shown in the list when the filter matches nothing

a11y.role: combobox, controlling a listbox that is aria-multiselectable
guarantees: React Aria's multi-select combobox: arrow keys move through the list while focus stays in the input, Enter or click toggles an option, and the list stays open for the next pick
the chosen labels are on the input's `aria-describedby`, joined by `Intl.ListFormat` — read with the field in the user's language, with no string shipped for it
the chosen values are a TagGroup named by the field's label: one tab stop, arrow keys between tags, Delete or the × to remove
Backspace in an empty field removes the last value; with text in the field it only edits the text
removing the last tag returns focus to the field instead of dropping it on <body>
`isRequired` marks the field required only while nothing is chosen — at least one
requires: `label`, or `aria-label` when there is no visible label — it names the tags as well as the field
notes: While the list is open, React Aria hides everything outside the field and the list from assistive technology, the tags included. That is the platform pattern for a combobox, not a defect: the chosen options are marked selected in the list itself.

antiPatterns.dont: a Combobox that appends each pick to a TagGroup by hand
antiPatterns.why: the list closes after every pick, the input shows the last label, and nothing announces what is chosen
it needs Ctrl or Cmd to pick a second option, which most people never discover, and it cannot filter

antiPatterns.dont: a count in place of the values — "3 selected"
antiPatterns.why: it hides which three; the tags show them and the field reads them

antiPatterns.dont: `hideTags` with nowhere else showing the values
antiPatterns.why: the field shows only the filter text, so the choice is invisible until the list is opened
